data.cultural_impact: The name "Peridot" may evoke images of this striking green gemstone, which has been valued for its beauty and rarity throughout history. In Islamic culture, this precious stone is believed to originate from the Red Sea, specifically from an island named Zabargad that is now called Topazio in the Red Sea. The island was known for its abundant deposits of Peridot.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic belief, the Peridot gemstone is considered a sacred stone, believed to bring good luck, success, and protection against evil. It is mentioned in the Hadith, sayings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), as one of the various gifts that the Prophet received from the people of the mountains. carrying a Peridot stone was believed to ward off the evil eye and protect the wearer from harm. In Sufism, the mystical branch of Islam, the Peridot stone is associated with the heart chakra, symbolizing love, compassion, and inner peace. Wearing or carrying a Peridot stone is thought to strengthen these qualities within oneself and help towards spiritual growth.
